title: Localization comparisons for the ringed projection mate
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R_Y$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and fix an identification $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and derived tensor computed by K-flat total complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For an object $V\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $U=X\times_YV$ and let $f_V$ be the induced morphism from the localized topos of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ at $U$ to that of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ at $V$. Write $j_V^*$ and $j_U^*$ for restriction to these localized sites and restrict the coefficient sheaves there. For $E\in D(R_X)$ and $P,M,N\in D(R_Y)$ there are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$j_V^*Rf_*E\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*E,\qquad j_U^*Lf^*P\cong Lf_V^*j_V^*P,\qquad j_V^*(M\otimes^L N)\cong j_V^*M\otimes^L j_V^*N.$$
Under these isomorphisms, restriction of the adjoint-of-counit projection map for $(f,E,P)$ is exactly the adjoint-of-counit projection map for $(f_V,j_U^*E,j_V^*P)$, including the canonical shift comparisons. A morphism in $D(R_Y)$ is an isomorphism if, for every site object $V$, some covering $\{V_i\to V\}$ makes all its restrictions to $V_i$ isomorphisms. No quasi-compactness or uniform cohomological bound is required.

The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical, and the proof dropped from 6953 to 2253 characters with no step over 2000. The DAG stays acyclic, including the new nodes. The item is not on the dropped list. Sources checked: Stacks 04J0 (sites-modules l.2368), 07A7 remark-base-change (sites-cohomology l.4033), and 08FI, 07A4, 0E48 and 0944 by their tags. Step 1 (localize-ringed-site-morphism with u_f(V)=X×_YV, exact restriction, termwise derived functors) is correct. Step 3 (tensor-pullback applied to j_V and j_U with identity coefficients, Lj^*=j^*) is correct. Step 5 is correct: the domains of the coverings form a small family whose sieve covers every V, so Sheaf.isIso_of_coversTop applies to the underlying abelian H^q(a); the inverse is linear, and the unbounded cohomology criterion finishes it with no boundedness hypothesis. Gap fixed (C3/E5): in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization, β is fixed by the right-derived unit square and θ is defined as its inverse mate (proof, ofMate). Its statement never ties θ to the ordinary localization square. Step 2's sentence 'counit compatibility makes β the mate of θ' is therefore a tautology. Step 4 needs θ to be the pullback comparison induced by the ringed commutation isomorphism, normalized on flat-term K-flat complexes as def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-square-presentation and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-square-tensor-compatibility require. That argument was the old Step 5, which the re-split dropped, and no cited statement supplies it. I added the statement-only node lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-pullback-mate-normalization (unsplit, created.item = the item, source 07A7+04J0+08FI). It states θ_qP = q(σ_P) on flat-term K-flat P, so β is the 07A7 base change map. Steps 2 and 4 and proof_deps are edited to cite it (proof now 2778 characters). I checked its sign convention against def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves: the A[n]⊗B map is the identity and the A⊗B[n] map is (-1)^{np}, and both differential parts commute for all n and p, so the statement is true. Its tensor clause overlaps the μ-shift clause of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact for f=j_V; this is advisory only, since that node's 'presented by small ringed sites' hypothesis is unclear for localizations of general sites.
